rationale: Both run the same correct depth-first search with the same six hex neighbours. B is more readable. It has a class docstring, a named NEIGHBOR_OFFSETS constant with a comment for each direction, descriptive names (height, width, seen, _reaches_opposite_edge) and an edge-test predicate in place of building a goal set. It also filters cells by player before pushing them onto the stack. Assigning lambdas to names is mildly unidiomatic (PEP 8 discourages it). B does not strip the input, so a board string with leading blank lines would break it, while A's strip() handles that. A is compact but terser, with an inline magic tuple of offsets. B's clearer naming and documentation give it the edge.
